title: Khufu cartouche allegedly painted by Vyse
summary: Jay Anderson tells of Khufu cartouche allegedly painted by Vyse, about 1830s at Egypt (no place named), and summarises it without a named source. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: This is like this 1800's explorer. I forgot his name like Voss or Vas something. And he was hired by uh the British Museum. He was running out of funding. He was running out of time. Lo and behold, he suddenly finds the signatures of Kufu written in very suspicious ochre.

plain: A researcher named Jay Anderson, talking on the podcast of host Jesse Michels, tells a story about the Great Pyramid of Giza in Egypt. He says an explorer in the 1800s, whose name he half remembers and whom the story names as Howard Vyse, was hired by the British Museum, was running out of money and time, and then suddenly found the name of Khufu, the ancient king usually credited with building the pyramid, written inside in what Anderson calls very suspicious ochre, a reddish earth paint. If that were so, one of the main written links between the pyramid and Khufu would be in doubt.
